🇲🇽✈️ <u>Day of the Dead + F1: foreign card spending up 41% in Mexico City</u>

Spending by foreign tourists with Visa cards rose 41% in Mexico City during the week of Día de Muertos and the Mexico City Grand Prix compared with the same week of 2025, according to a Visa analysis released by Sectur and reported by El Economista. In Pátzcuaro, Oaxaca and Puebla it jumped about 109%; nationwide, 17%. "When more tourists arrive, there are more opportunities for our restaurants, hotels, shops and the families who live off tourism," said Tourism Secretary Josefina Rodríguez Zamora.

🇲🇽📊 <u>World Bank: 17.3 million Mexicans out of poverty since 2018</u>

Monetary poverty in Mexico fell from 43.9 million people in 2018 to 26.6 million in 2026, according to World Bank estimates. The rate dropped from 35.3% to 20%. The bank credits rising real labor incomes and social programs reaching more households, and projects poverty could fall to 18.7% by 2028 if the trend holds. The 2025-2026 figures are projections built on data observed through 2024.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>2006: the Tribunal reopened 9% of polling stations and found 70% altered</u>

Former IFE chief Luis Carlos Ugalde says the 2006 fraud accusations are "unfounded" because the Electoral Tribunal already "declared that election valid." Contralínea looks at what that Tribunal actually did: it refused a full recount and reviewed only 9% of polling stations. In that sample, 7,442 stations, 70% of those opened, showed substantial alterations: 45,890 surplus votes in 3,074 stations and 80,392 missing ballots in 4,368 others. The Tribunal certified the result anyway. Calderón's official margin: 0.56 points.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>Harfuch after DEA meeting: cooperation, not subordination</u>

Security Secretary Omar García Harfuch said the meeting with DEA director Terrance Cole was a routine review scheduled three months in advance, part of check-ins held every three or four months with the DEA, the FBI and other US agencies. Extradition requests from both sides and ongoing investigations were on the table. Asked whether Cole made any specific demand, Harfuch answered: "nothing specific, nothing extraordinary." Sheinbaum added that Mexico does not share Washington's "narcoterrorism" label: under Mexican law, these groups are prosecuted as organized crime.

🇲🇽🇨🇳 <u>Chinese business chamber calls Sheinbaum's trip "great news"</u>

Sheinbaum heads to the APEC summit in Shenzhen, with a bilateral meeting with Xi Jinping on Tuesday the 17th and a keynote before the APEC Business Advisory Council, more than 1,000 executives from 21 economies. The Mexico-China Chamber of Commerce and Technology (ChinaCham) called the visit "great news" because it "renews momentum for investment, trade and technological cooperation," while asking for "national treatment and non-discrimination" for Chinese firms operating legally in Mexico. Mexico has already ruled out an FTA with Beijing and says the T-MEC is untouched. Plan México goes to Asia anyway.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>Mexico's poppy fields shrink 27.65% in one year, UN confirms</u>

Opium poppy cultivation in Mexico fell from 11,095 hectares in 2022-2023 to 8,028 in 2023-2024, according to the seventh joint Mexico–UNODC monitoring report presented November 13. Potential opium gum output dropped 36.48%, from 166.31 to 105.64 tonnes. The report links the decline to the shift toward synthetic opioids and to income support for farmers in Guerrero, Sinaloa, Nayarit, Chihuahua and Durango, including Sembrando Vida. Federal forces also eradicated 9,087 hectares in 2024.

🇲🇽💰 <u>Minimum wage 2027: bosses offer 9%, unions want 12%, government aims above 10%</u>

Mexico's minimum-wage commission (Conasami) opens its permanent session November 23–27 and can vote from December 1. Employers led by Coparmex want to cap the raise at 9–9.9%, or inflation plus one point. The CROC union is asking for 12%. The government side projects more than 10%, on track for a minimum wage worth 2.5 urban basic baskets by 2030, El Economista reports. Today the general minimum wage covers 1.93 times the urban income-poverty line, and 2.7 times in the northern border zone.

🇲🇽🩺 <u>Doctors Without Borders in Mexico City: for torture survivors, "trauma speaks through the body"</u>

In ten years, Médecins Sans Frontières' Comprehensive Care Center in Mexico City has treated 1,205 patients and given more than 23,200 specialized consultations, many of them to migrants who fled violence at home and met more on the route north. Its caseload includes 156 cases of torture, 137 of kidnapping and 241 of sexual violence. One patient, Tamara, fled gang threats in Honduras: "I had to play dead for 15 minutes so they would stop beating me."

🚨🇲🇽 <u>"Shield of the Americas": Washington's 14-country bloc, and why Mexico isn't in it</u>

Fourteen governments, from Milei's Argentina to Bukele's El Salvador, have joined Trump's "Shield of the Americas," and in September Washington revived the Rio Treaty (TIAR), the Cold War mutual-defense pact, to build a regional coalition against "narco-terrorism." Costa Rica and Argentina have already designated Mexican cartels as terrorist groups. Contralínea's investigation argues the real target is critical minerals and oil, and asks whether that coalition would strike cartels in third countries, Mexico included. Sheinbaum's answer on November 3: "Terrorism is something else… it cannot be a pretext for invasion or interference by any country in ours."
